metadata.title: PISA 2012 Results: What Makes Schools Successful (Volume IV) (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2012 volume reports results based on the PISA 2012 assessment of 15-year-olds across 65 countries and economies, using PISA’s standard complex survey design. The excerpt specifies that when school-principal responses are presented, they are weighted to be proportionate to the number of 15-year-olds enrolled in the school, indicating the use of weighting at least for school-level questionnaire responses. The provided text does not name the specific student weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or any replicate-weight scheme, so the exact weight variable(s) and variance estimation method cannot be extracted from the supplied section. For analysts reusing the underlying PISA microdata, the recommended practice is to apply the official PISA sampling/survey weights and replicate weights (if available in the dataset) when producing standard errors and confidence intervals, and to use the appropriate school-level weights for school questionnaire indicators.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The provided excerpt does not describe any plausible-values (PV) generation or PV-based modeling strategy, and it is a descriptive policy volume summarising relationships and trends rather than reporting an ML model with an explicit PV pipeline. While PISA uses PVs for cognitive achievement scales in general, this specific volume section does not document how PVs were handled for the reported indicators. Missing-data handling is also not specified in the excerpt beyond the reporting symbols (e.g., categories not applying, too few observations, data not available/withdrawn), so a detailed imputation/deletion rule cannot be extracted from the text provided.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: PISA 2012 targets 15-year-old students (15 years 3 months to 16 years 2 months) who are enrolled in school and have completed at least 6 years of formal schooling, regardless of programme type or school sector. The excerpt states that exclusions are governed by strict technical standards and that the overall exclusion rate within a country was required to be below 5% to limit distortions in national mean scores. The provided text does not specify additional analytic restrictions (e.g., grade-only, subject-only, or complete-case rules) for the specific volume’s reported indicators; therefore, for this extraction, the analytic sample is treated as the full available PISA 2012 target population for the specified countries and economies.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD volume reports policy-oriented results from PISA 2012, focusing on how resources, policies, and practices relate to education outcomes, with emphasis on mathematics performance and equity. PISA 2012 assessed around 510,000 15-year-old students across 65 countries and economies using paper-based tests (about two hours) and, in some systems, an additional computer-based component. The report links student, school, and system indicators through questionnaires completed by students and school principals (and sometimes parents), and it highlights statistically significant differences and trends between 2003 and 2012 where comparable data exist. The excerpt does not provide an explicit PV-handling or missing-data imputation strategy for any specific model, and it does not describe any machine-learning predictive pipeline; instead, it synthesizes descriptive and multilevel relationships for policy interpretation. Consequently, the findings should be interpreted as evidence of associations and system-level patterns rather than causal effects of specific policies.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2012 results volume (Volume IV) that synthesizes relationships between education outcomes and system/school characteristics for policy discussion, rather than presenting an ML predictive modeling study with a documented algorithmic pipeline. As a result, there are no extractable ML techniques, PV-handling details, or target-variable-specific predictive performance metrics in the provided text. The excerpt also does not report per-country analytic sample sizes or a specific analytic subsample definition beyond the PISA target population and general exclusion-rate requirements, so country-level n_students cannot be populated from the supplied section.
